title: The left-tuned schedule family, in the machine: T4OffL section S7 - t4l_schedA(sigma) = (9999/2)^{1/sigma}, per-point closure of the first T4 term at every schedule at or above the critical scale, and the proof that NO d0-uniform schedule exists

Declarations: (1) S7.1 t4l_schedA (sigma : R) := (9999/2:R)^(1/sigma) - the critical scale constant: at B = A(sigma)*t^{2/sigma} the first T4 term computes (1/2)*B^{-sigma} = (1/2)*(A(sigma)^{-sigma})*t^{-2} = (1/2)*(2/9999)*t^{-2} = (1/9999)*t^{-2} - EXACTLY the edge-floor scale target, no slack, no numeric pin. (2) S7.2 t4l_schedA_pos - well-defined and positive for every sigma > 0. (3) S7.3 t4l_schedTerm1 (t >= 1000, sigma > 0) : for EVERY schedule n with (n:R) >= A(sigma)*t^{2/sigma}, (1/2)*n^{-sigma} <= (1/9999)*t^{-2} - the per-point closure of the first T4 term at or above the critical scale; the proof is an identity chain (mul_rpow / rpow_mul bridges / rpow_neg / inv-le-inv), no numeric exp. (4) S7.4 t4l_schedBeat4pin : (9999/2)^200 * 10^40 > 62000000^99 (PURE norm_num) and t4l_schedBeat4 : at t = 10^10 and the band edge sigma = 99/200 the critical scale A(sigma)*t^{400/99} = (9999/2)^{200/99}*t^{400/99} STRICTLY EXCEEDS the uniform machine schedule S4Strip.n4 (<= 2*3.1e7*t^4 via t4l_n4upper) - by_contra + 99th-power pin; the dual statement of t4l_barrier_edge as a schedule comparison instead of a term-floor comparison. (5) S7.5 t4l_schedDiverge : for EVERY A > 0 there exists d0 in [1/200, 1/2) with t4l_schedA (1/2 - d0) > A - explicit choice sigma = min(ln(9999/2)/(2 ln A), 1/2000), d0 = 1/2 - sigma: the schedule then exceeds A^2 > A; the A <= 1 case is the band edge itself (1 < schedA(99/200) by one_lt_rpow). CONSEQUENCE: the tuned constant is UNBOUNDED as d0 approaches 1/2 (sigma -> 0) - no schedule with a d0-UNIFORM leading constant (hence no uniform n-polynomial schedule) can serve the left wire across the band; per-point tuning is ESSENTIAL, and it is exactly what the S3 squeeze at a left-flank witness requires.

why_it_matters: The 0121 barriers were formal NEGATIVE statements: the uniform n4 wire cannot close the S3 face at sigma < 1/2 (edge barrier t >= 10^10; sigma0 barrier at d0 = 1/2). A barrier without its dual leaves the next question unanswered: what WOULD close it? S7 answers in the machine: (a) the exact per-point schedule - run n at or above A(sigma)*t^{2/sigma} with A(sigma) = (9999/2)^{1/sigma} - closes the FIRST T4 term at the edge-floor scale with an exact identity, no slack; (b) why the machine's uniform schedule cannot do it - at the frontier height the critical scale strictly exceeds n4 (S7.4, pinned to a norm_num-able 99th power); and (c) why NO uniform schedule can ever do it - the required constant diverges as the witness approaches d0 = 1/2 (S7.5). This converts G-hs3-left from 'the wire is too weak' into 'the wire is the wrong KIND: the obligation is per-point and the per-point schedule is explicit' - a cleaner, and more actionable, statement of the residual. It also sets the shape of any future closure attempt: a proof that the FULL S3 squeeze holds at the per-point tuned schedule (analytic, the face) - the machine now holds the schedule-side arithmetic ready to consume it.
